questions.question: What is the driving force and curved-arrow flow during chain propagation in the radical polymerization of styrene?

options.label: A
options.text: The radical attacks the benzene ring carbons directly.

options.label: B
options.text: Styrene polymerizes via a pericyclic [2+2] cycloaddition.

options.label: C
options.text: The radical undergoes homolytic cleavage to phenyl radicals.

options.label: D
options.text: The propagating carbon radical attacks the terminal =CH₂ carbon of a styrene monomer, forming a new C-C σ bond and generating a new, resonance-stabilized benzylic radical.

questions.correct_answer: The propagating carbon radical attacks the terminal =CH₂ carbon of a styrene monomer, forming a new C-C σ bond and generating a new, resonance-stabilized benzylic radical.
questions.explanation: Radical addition occurs regioselectively at the terminal methylene to generate the more stable, resonance-delocalized benzylic radical.

questions.question: Why does 2-methylpropene (isobutylene) undergo rapid cationic polymerization with BF₃/H₂O but fail under anionic conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: Isobutylene has no double bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: BF₃ is a radical inhibitor.

options.label: C
options.text: Protonation generates an exceptionally stable tertiary carbocation [(CH₃)₃C⁺] that propagates efficiently; isobutylene cannot form or stabilize a carbanion intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: Isobutylene is an aromatic monomer.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation generates an exceptionally stable tertiary carbocation [(CH₃)₃C⁺] that propagates efficiently; isobutylene cannot form or stabilize a carbanion intermediate.
questions.explanation: Electron-donating alkyl groups stabilize carbocation intermediates, making isobutylene an ideal monomer for cationic (acid-initiated) polymerization.

questions.question: Why does methyl methacrylate (MMA) polymerize smoothly with n-butyllithium (BuLi) via an anionic mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: BuLi oxidizes the ester to a radical cation.

options.label: B
options.text: Anionic polymerization requires high-energy gamma rays.

options.label: C
options.text: MMA is an acid that protonates butyllithium.

options.label: D
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the carbanion on the terminal alkene generates an ester-stabilized enolate carbanion [CH₂-C⁻(CH₃)COOCH₃] that propagates the anionic chain.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the carbanion on the terminal alkene generates an ester-stabilized enolate carbanion [CH₂-C⁻(CH₃)COOCH₃] that propagates the anionic chain.
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing ester carbonyl groups delocalize and stabilize the propagating carbanion as a resonance-stabilized enolate.

questions.question: How does the heterogeneous TiCl₄ / AlEt₃ Ziegler-Natta catalyst produce 100% isotactic polypropylene?

options.label: A
options.text: The catalyst forms free radicals in solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Propylene coordinates to a vacant d-orbital on the chiral titanium metal center, which directs stereospecific syn-migratory insertion into the growing titanium-alkyl polymer chain.

options.label: C
options.text: The catalyst dissolves the propylene into liquid crystals.

options.label: D
options.text: The catalyst heats the reaction to 500°C.

questions.correct_answer: Propylene coordinates to a vacant d-orbital on the chiral titanium metal center, which directs stereospecific syn-migratory insertion into the growing titanium-alkyl polymer chain.
questions.explanation: Coordination of the monomer to the well-defined, asymmetric titanium coordination sphere dictates stereospecific facial insertion, forging pure isotactic polymer.

questions.question: What is the elementary mechanistic step in the industrial synthesis of Nylon-6,6 from adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine at 280°C?

options.label: A
options.text: Nucleophilic acyl substitution: the primary amine attacks the carboxylic acid carbonyl to form an amide bond, with continuous thermal elimination and removal of water.

options.label: B
options.text: Ring-opening metathesis of a cyclic lactam.

options.label: C
options.text: Coordination insertion into a titanium catalyst.

options.label: D
options.text: Radical chain addition across double bonds.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic acyl substitution: the primary amine attacks the carboxylic acid carbonyl to form an amide bond, with continuous thermal elimination and removal of water.
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is formed by step-growth polyamidation between bifunctional diacids and diamines with continuous removal of water byproduct.

questions.question: What are the stoichiometric byproducts removed during the industrial melt polymerization of PET from dimethyl terephthalate and ethylene glycol?

options.label: A
options.text: Ammonia gas.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethylene gas and hydrochloric acid.

options.label: C
options.text: Methanol (CH₃OH) gas is continuously removed by vacuum during transesterification, driving the step-growth condensation equilibrium toward high molecular weight polyester.

options.label: D
options.text: Water and carbon dioxide.

questions.correct_answer: Methanol (CH₃OH) gas is continuously removed by vacuum during transesterification, driving the step-growth condensation equilibrium toward high molecular weight polyester.
questions.explanation: Transesterification between dimethyl terephthalate and ethylene glycol expels volatile methanol, which is distilled off under vacuum.

questions.topic: Kevlar Aramid High Tensile Strength Mechanism
questions.question: What molecular and supramolecular interactions give Kevlar (poly-p-phenylene terephthalamide) its bullet-resistant strength?

options.label: A
options.text: Covalent diamond-like sp³ carbon networks.

options.label: B
options.text: Ionic bonds between sodium and chloride.

options.label: C
options.text: Flexible aliphatic coils that stretch like rubber bands.

options.label: D
options.text: Rigid, planar aromatic rings in a fully extended trans-polyamide conformation form an extensive, dense network of intermolecular hydrogen bonds between adjacent polymer sheets.

questions.correct_answer: Rigid, planar aromatic rings in a fully extended trans-polyamide conformation form an extensive, dense network of intermolecular hydrogen bonds between adjacent polymer sheets.
questions.explanation: Rigid linear aromatic backbones stack into crystalline sheets locked together by regular, dense arrays of intermolecular N-H···O=C hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: What is the nucleophilic substitution mechanism in the synthesis of Lexan polycarbonate from bisphenol A and phosgene?

options.label: A
options.text: Deprotonated phenoxide oxygens of bisphenol A attack the electrophilic carbonyl of phosgene (COCl₂) in sequential addition-eliminations, expelling two chloride ions per linkage.

options.label: B
options.text: Ring-closing metathesis with loss of ethylene.

options.label: C
options.text: Free radical polymerization of bisphenol A double bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Coordination polymerization with titanium catalysts.

questions.correct_answer: Deprotonated phenoxide oxygens of bisphenol A attack the electrophilic carbonyl of phosgene (COCl₂) in sequential addition-eliminations, expelling two chloride ions per linkage.
questions.explanation: Interfacial polycondensation between bisphenol A phenoxide and phosgene expels chloride in repeated nucleophilic acyl substitution steps.

questions.question: What is the chemical role of elemental sulfur (S₈) and zinc oxide during the vulcanization of natural rubber?

options.label: A
options.text: Sulfur hydrogenates all double bonds to single bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: Sulfur dissolves the rubber into liquid latex.

options.label: C
options.text: Sulfur cleaves polyisoprene into monomeric isoprene units.

options.label: D
options.text: Sulfur radicals abstract allylic hydrogens from cis-1,4-polyisoprene chains, creating allylic radicals that couple with polysulfide chains to form covalent -Sₙ- crosslinks between chains.

questions.correct_answer: Sulfur radicals abstract allylic hydrogens from cis-1,4-polyisoprene chains, creating allylic radicals that couple with polysulfide chains to form covalent -Sₙ- crosslinks between chains.
questions.explanation: Thermal reaction with sulfur forms covalent polysulfide bridges between polyisoprene chains at allylic positions, preventing chain slippage (converting gummy latex to resilient rubber).

questions.question: What is the chemical mechanism of PET plastic bottle recycling via catalytic glycolysis?

options.label: A
options.text: Acid leaching of dyes without breaking polymer bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: Excess ethylene glycol in the presence of a zinc acetate catalyst undergoes transesterification with PET ester linkages, depolymerizing the long polyester back to pure BHET monomer.

options.label: C
options.text: Pyrolysis of PET to carbon black.

options.label: D
options.text: Complete combustion of PET to CO₂ and water.

questions.correct_answer: Excess ethylene glycol in the presence of a zinc acetate catalyst undergoes transesterification with PET ester linkages, depolymerizing the long polyester back to pure BHET monomer.
questions.explanation: Catalytic transesterification with excess ethylene glycol depolymerizes the PET polymer back to bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) monomer for closed-loop polymerization.

questions.question: What is the driving force and curved-arrow flow during chain propagation in the radical polymerization of styrene?

options.label: A
options.text: The radical undergoes homolytic cleavage to phenyl radicals.

options.label: B
options.text: The radical attacks the benzene ring carbons directly.

options.label: C
options.text: Styrene polymerizes via a pericyclic [2+2] cycloaddition.

options.label: D
options.text: The propagating carbon radical attacks the terminal =CH₂ carbon of a styrene monomer, forming a new C-C σ bond and generating a new, resonance-stabilized benzylic radical.

questions.correct_answer: The propagating carbon radical attacks the terminal =CH₂ carbon of a styrene monomer, forming a new C-C σ bond and generating a new, resonance-stabilized benzylic radical.
questions.explanation: Radical addition occurs regioselectively at the terminal methylene to generate the more stable, resonance-delocalized benzylic radical.

questions.question: Why does 2-methylpropene (isobutylene) undergo rapid cationic polymerization with BF₃/H₂O but fail under anionic conditions?

options.label: A
options.text: Protonation generates an exceptionally stable tertiary carbocation [(CH₃)₃C⁺] that propagates efficiently; isobutylene cannot form or stabilize a carbanion intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: BF₃ is a radical inhibitor.

options.label: C
options.text: Isobutylene is an aromatic monomer.

options.label: D
options.text: Isobutylene has no double bonds.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation generates an exceptionally stable tertiary carbocation [(CH₃)₃C⁺] that propagates efficiently; isobutylene cannot form or stabilize a carbanion intermediate.
questions.explanation: Electron-donating alkyl groups stabilize carbocation intermediates, making isobutylene an ideal monomer for cationic (acid-initiated) polymerization.

questions.question: Why does methyl methacrylate (MMA) polymerize smoothly with n-butyllithium (BuLi) via an anionic mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Nucleophilic attack of the carbanion on the terminal alkene generates an ester-stabilized enolate carbanion [CH₂-C⁻(CH₃)COOCH₃] that propagates the anionic chain.

options.label: B
options.text: MMA is an acid that protonates butyllithium.

options.label: C
options.text: Anionic polymerization requires high-energy gamma rays.

options.label: D
options.text: BuLi oxidizes the ester to a radical cation.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic attack of the carbanion on the terminal alkene generates an ester-stabilized enolate carbanion [CH₂-C⁻(CH₃)COOCH₃] that propagates the anionic chain.
questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing ester carbonyl groups delocalize and stabilize the propagating carbanion as a resonance-stabilized enolate.

questions.question: How does the heterogeneous TiCl₄ / AlEt₃ Ziegler-Natta catalyst produce 100% isotactic polypropylene?

options.label: A
options.text: The catalyst heats the reaction to 500°C.

options.label: B
options.text: The catalyst dissolves the propylene into liquid crystals.

options.label: C
options.text: Propylene coordinates to a vacant d-orbital on the chiral titanium metal center, which directs stereospecific syn-migratory insertion into the growing titanium-alkyl polymer chain.

options.label: D
options.text: The catalyst forms free radicals in solution.

questions.correct_answer: Propylene coordinates to a vacant d-orbital on the chiral titanium metal center, which directs stereospecific syn-migratory insertion into the growing titanium-alkyl polymer chain.
questions.explanation: Coordination of the monomer to the well-defined, asymmetric titanium coordination sphere dictates stereospecific facial insertion, forging pure isotactic polymer.

questions.question: What is the elementary mechanistic step in the industrial synthesis of Nylon-6,6 from adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine at 280°C?

options.label: A
options.text: Ring-opening metathesis of a cyclic lactam.

options.label: B
options.text: Coordination insertion into a titanium catalyst.

options.label: C
options.text: Radical chain addition across double bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Nucleophilic acyl substitution: the primary amine attacks the carboxylic acid carbonyl to form an amide bond, with continuous thermal elimination and removal of water.

questions.correct_answer: Nucleophilic acyl substitution: the primary amine attacks the carboxylic acid carbonyl to form an amide bond, with continuous thermal elimination and removal of water.
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is formed by step-growth polyamidation between bifunctional diacids and diamines with continuous removal of water byproduct.

questions.question: What are the stoichiometric byproducts removed during the industrial melt polymerization of PET from dimethyl terephthalate and ethylene glycol?

options.label: A
options.text: Ammonia gas.

options.label: B
options.text: Water and carbon dioxide.

options.label: C
options.text: Methanol (CH₃OH) gas is continuously removed by vacuum during transesterification, driving the step-growth condensation equilibrium toward high molecular weight polyester.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethylene gas and hydrochloric acid.

questions.correct_answer: Methanol (CH₃OH) gas is continuously removed by vacuum during transesterification, driving the step-growth condensation equilibrium toward high molecular weight polyester.
questions.explanation: Transesterification between dimethyl terephthalate and ethylene glycol expels volatile methanol, which is distilled off under vacuum.

questions.question: What is the chemical role of elemental sulfur (S₈) and zinc oxide during the vulcanization of natural rubber?

options.label: A
options.text: Sulfur dissolves the rubber into liquid latex.

options.label: B
options.text: Sulfur hydrogenates all double bonds to single bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: Sulfur cleaves polyisoprene into monomeric isoprene units.

options.label: D
options.text: Sulfur radicals abstract allylic hydrogens from cis-1,4-polyisoprene chains, creating allylic radicals that couple with polysulfide chains to form covalent -Sₙ- crosslinks between chains.

questions.correct_answer: Sulfur radicals abstract allylic hydrogens from cis-1,4-polyisoprene chains, creating allylic radicals that couple with polysulfide chains to form covalent -Sₙ- crosslinks between chains.
questions.explanation: Thermal reaction with sulfur forms covalent polysulfide bridges between polyisoprene chains at allylic positions, preventing chain slippage (converting gummy latex to resilient rubber).

questions.topic: Kevlar Aramid High Tensile Strength Mechanism
questions.question: What molecular and supramolecular interactions give Kevlar (poly-p-phenylene terephthalamide) its bullet-resistant strength?

options.label: A
options.text: Covalent diamond-like sp³ carbon networks.

options.label: B
options.text: Flexible aliphatic coils that stretch like rubber bands.

options.label: C
options.text: Ionic bonds between sodium and chloride.

options.label: D
options.text: Rigid, planar aromatic rings in a fully extended trans-polyamide conformation form an extensive, dense network of intermolecular hydrogen bonds between adjacent polymer sheets.

questions.correct_answer: Rigid, planar aromatic rings in a fully extended trans-polyamide conformation form an extensive, dense network of intermolecular hydrogen bonds between adjacent polymer sheets.
questions.explanation: Rigid linear aromatic backbones stack into crystalline sheets locked together by regular, dense arrays of intermolecular N-H···O=C hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: What is the nucleophilic substitution mechanism in the synthesis of Lexan polycarbonate from bisphenol A and phosgene?

options.label: A
options.text: Free radical polymerization of bisphenol A double bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: Deprotonated phenoxide oxygens of bisphenol A attack the electrophilic carbonyl of phosgene (COCl₂) in sequential addition-eliminations, expelling two chloride ions per linkage.

options.label: C
options.text: Coordination polymerization with titanium catalysts.

options.label: D
options.text: Ring-closing metathesis with loss of ethylene.

questions.correct_answer: Deprotonated phenoxide oxygens of bisphenol A attack the electrophilic carbonyl of phosgene (COCl₂) in sequential addition-eliminations, expelling two chloride ions per linkage.
questions.explanation: Interfacial polycondensation between bisphenol A phenoxide and phosgene expels chloride in repeated nucleophilic acyl substitution steps.
